Summary

Math.js exposes an expression-evaluation API (math.evaluate) intended to run untrusted mathematical expressions inside a restricted sandbox that blocks access to dangerous properties such as constructor. The isSafeProperty guard only inspects direct property access performed from the user-supplied expression text, but does not cover accesses made through internal library code paths. By abusing the reviver deserialization helper to reconstruct an ArrayNode, leaking its internal array via toJSON(), and overwriting the array’s .map method with an attacker-controlled function, an attacker can trick Math.js’s own internal code into calling Function.constructor, escaping the sandbox and reaching arbitrary JavaScript execution. The included Docker lab and server.js provide a minimal vulnerable Node.js service that accepts a math expression and evaluates it, letting the PoC payload pop a reverse shell on the host.
